title: First order thickenings are exactly square-zero quasi-coherent ideal extensions of the structure sheaf
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises first order thickenings over a base algebraically: a short exact sequence 0 -> I -> A -> O_X -> 0 of sheaves on X with A a sheaf of f^{-1}O_S-algebras, I of square zero and I quasi-coherent as an O_X-module makes X' = (X, A) a scheme and X -> X' a first order thickening over S, and every first order thickening arises this way (statement lines 93-108). The substance is the local computation: on an affine open U = Spec(B) the vanishing of H^1(U, I) makes A = Gamma(U, A) -> B surjective, and the candidate isomorphism (U, A|_U) -> Spec(A) has to be checked on local rings, which is done by comparing two short exact sequences whose outer arrows are isomorphisms precisely because I and O_X are quasi-coherent (proof lines 112-150). The author leaves the converse direction implicit and it is reproduced as written. The claim is H2: a genuine local-ring computation with one vanishing input, not a citation.
